topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumOf
description: Returns the total using long arithmetic; returns 0 for a null or empty array.
code_b: public static long sumOf(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0; } long sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { sum += values[i]; } return sum; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageOf
description: Returns the arithmetic mean; returns 0.0 for a null or empty array. The calculation uses Java double arithmetic.
code_b: public static double averageOf(double[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0.0; } double sum = 0.0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { sum += values[i]; } return sum / values.length; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countNegative
description: Returns the number of negative elements; returns 0 for a null or empty array.
code_b: public static int countNegative(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < 0) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countInRange
signature: public static int countInRange(double[] values, double lower, double upper)
description: Counts elements between lower and upper, inclusive; returns 0 for a null or empty array or when lower is greater than upper. NaN elements and NaN bounds are not counted because the comparisons are false.
code_b: public static int countInRange(double[] values, double lower, double upper) { if (values == null || values.length == 0 || lower > upper) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] >= lower && values[i] <= upper) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumBeforeFirstNegative
description: Returns the sum of elements before the first negative element; returns 0 for a null or empty array or if the first element is negative. The sum uses long arithmetic.
code_b: public static long sumBeforeFirstNegative(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0; } long sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < 0) { break; } sum += values[i]; } return sum; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countZeros
description: Returns the number of elements equal to zero; returns 0 for a null or empty array. Both positive and negative zero count as zero; NaN does not.
code_b: public static int countZeros(double[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] == 0.0) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countNonNegative
description: Returns the number of elements that are positive or zero; returns 0 for a null or empty array. NaN is not counted.
code_b: public static int countNonNegative(double[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] >= 0.0) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumMatrix
description: Returns the sum of all elements, using long arithmetic; returns 0 for a null or empty matrix and ignores null rows. An empty row contributes nothing.
code_b: public static long sumMatrix(int[][] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return 0; } long sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] != null) { for (int j = 0; j < values[i].length; j++) { sum += values[i][j]; } } } return sum; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumPositive
description: Returns the sum of values greater than zero; null and empty arrays return 0.0. NaN values are not included because they are not greater than zero.
code_b: public static double sumPositive(double[] values) { if (values == null) return 0.0; double sum = 0.0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] > 0.0) sum += values[i]; } return sum; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countEven
description: Returns the number of even integers in the array. Null and empty arrays return 0.
code_b: public static int countEven(int[] values) { if (values == null) return 0; int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] % 2 == 0) count++; } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averagePositive
description: Returns the average of values greater than zero; null and empty arrays return 0.0. It also returns 0.0 when the array has no positive values.
code_b: public static double averagePositive(double[] values) { if (values == null) return 0.0; double sum = 0.0; int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] > 0.0) { sum += values[i]; count++; } } if (count == 0) return 0.0; return sum / count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: cumulativeSums
description: Returns an array where each position contains the running total through that position in the input. Null and empty arrays return an empty array.
code_b: public static int[] cumulativeSums(int[] values) { if (values == null) return new int[0]; int[] sums = new int[values.length]; int total = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { total += values[i]; sums[i] = total; } return sums; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countTrue
description: Returns the number of true values in the array. Null and empty arrays return 0.
code_b: public static int countTrue(boolean[] values) { if (values == null) return 0; int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i]) count++; } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumAtEvenIndexes
description: Returns the sum of values at indexes 0, 2, 4, and so on. Null and empty arrays return 0.
code_b: public static int sumAtEvenIndexes(int[] values) { if (values == null) return 0; int sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i += 2) { sum += values[i]; } return sum; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: rowSums
description: Returns an array containing the sum of each row. A null matrix returns an empty array, and a null row contributes 0.
code_b: public static int[] rowSums(int[][] values) { if (values == null) return new int[0]; int[] sums = new int[values.length]; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] != null) { for (int j = 0; j < values[i].length; j++) { sums[i] += values[i][j]; } } } return sums; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: adjacentRelationCounts
description: Returns three counts in order: increasing adjacent pairs, equal adjacent pairs, and decreasing adjacent pairs. Null arrays and arrays with fewer than two elements return {0, 0, 0}.
code_b: public static int[] adjacentRelationCounts(int[] values) { int[] counts = new int[3]; if (values == null || values.length < 2) return counts; for (int i = 0; i < values.length - 1; i++) { if (values[i] < values[i + 1]) counts[0]++; else if (values[i] == values[i + 1]) counts[1]++; else counts[2]++; } return counts; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countOccurrences
signature: public static int countOccurrences(int[] values, int target)
description: Returns the number of elements equal to target. A null or empty array returns 0.
code_b: public static int countOccurrences(int[] values, int target) { int count = 0; if (values == null) { return 0; } for (int value : values) { if (value == target) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumOddIndexedValues
description: Returns the sum of elements at odd indexes (1, 3, 5, and so on). A null or empty array returns 0.
code_b: public static long sumOddIndexedValues(int[] values) { long sum = 0; if (values == null) { return 0; } for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i += 2) { sum += values[i]; } return sum; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageEvenValues
description: Returns the average of the even-valued elements. A null array or an array with no even values returns 0.0.
code_b: public static double averageEvenValues(int[] values) { if (values == null) { return 0.0; } long sum = 0; int count = 0; for (int value : values) { if (value % 2 == 0) { sum += value; count++; } } if (count == 0) { return 0.0; } return (double) sum / count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countUntilStop
signature: public static int countUntilStop(char[] values, char stop, char target)
description: Counts target characters before the first stop character; the stop character itself is not counted. A null or empty array returns 0, and if stop equals target, the count is 0.
code_b: public static int countUntilStop(char[] values, char stop, char target) { if (values == null || stop == target) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (char value : values) { if (value == stop) { break; } if (value == target) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countStartingWith
signature: public static int countStartingWith(String[] words, String prefix)
description: Counts non-null strings that start with prefix. A null array or null prefix returns 0; an empty array returns 0, and an empty prefix matches every non-null string.
code_b: public static int countStartingWith(String[] words, String prefix) { if (words == null || prefix == null) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (String word : words) { if (word != null && word.startsWith(prefix)) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageNonNullStringLength
description: Returns the average length of the non-null strings; empty strings are included with length 0. A null or empty array, or an array containing only nulls, returns 0.0.
code_b: public static double averageNonNullStringLength(String[] words) { if (words == null) { return 0.0; } long totalLength = 0; int count = 0; for (String word : words) { if (word != null) { totalLength += word.length(); count++; } } if (count == 0) { return 0.0; } return (double) totalLength / count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countRowDivisibleValues
description: Counts elements in each row that are divisible by that row's one-based number (row 0 uses divisor 1). A null matrix, empty matrix, or null or empty row contributes nothing.
code_b: public static int countRowDivisibleValues(int[][] values) { if (values == null) { return 0; } int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] != null) { for (int value : values[i]) { if (value % (i + 1) == 0) { count++; } } } } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countAtOrBelowPreviousAverage
description: Counts elements, starting at index 1, that are at or below the average of all earlier elements. A null or empty array returns 0; an array with one element also returns 0.
code_b: public static int countAtOrBelowPreviousAverage(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length < 2) { return 0; } long sum = values[0]; int count = 0; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { double average = (double) sum / i; if (values[i] <= average) { count++; } sum += values[i]; } return count; }

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumEveryThirdValue
description: Returns the sum of values at indexes 0, 3, 6, and so on. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageAboveThreshold
signature: public static double averageAboveThreshold(int[] values, int threshold)
description: Returns the average of values strictly greater than the threshold. Returns 0.0 for a null or empty array, or when no values qualify.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countMaximumValues
description: Returns how many array elements equal the largest value in the array. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countPrimeValues
description: Counts the prime numbers in the array; values below 2 are not prime. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageAbsoluteDeviation
description: Returns the average absolute distance of the elements from their arithmetic mean. Returns 0.0 for a null or empty array.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countNonEmptyStrings
description: Counts strings that are not null and have at least one character; whitespace-only strings count. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumMainDiagonal
description: Sums matrix[i][i] for each row where that diagonal element exists; null rows are skipped. Returns 0 for a null or empty matrix.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countDistinctValues
description: Returns the number of different integer values in the array. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumAbsoluteValues
description: Returns the sum of the absolute values; returns 0.0 for a null or empty array. If an element is NaN, the result is NaN.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageNegativeValues
description: Returns the average of the negative elements; returns 0.0 for a null or empty array, or when there are no negative elements.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countAboveAverage
description: Counts elements strictly greater than the array's arithmetic mean; returns 0 for a null or empty array. If the mean is NaN, including when the array contains NaN, no elements are counted.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumValuesBelow
signature: public static long sumValuesBelow(int[] values, int limit)
description: Returns the sum of elements strictly less than limit; returns 0 for a null or empty array. The total is accumulated as a long.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: averageAtEvenIndexes
description: Returns the average of elements at indexes 0, 2, 4, and so on; returns 0.0 for a null or empty array. A nonempty array always has at least one such index.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countPositiveAtOddIndexes
description: Counts positive elements at odd indexes (1, 3, 5, and so on); returns 0 for a null or empty array. NaN elements are not counted as positive.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: countRowsContainingNonzero
description: Counts rows containing at least one nonzero element; returns 0 for a null or empty matrix. Null and empty rows are treated as rows containing no nonzero elements.

topic: running totals, averages and counts over int or double arrays
name: sumClampedValues
signature: public static double sumClampedValues(double[] values, double lowerBound, double upperBound)
description: Adds each element after limiting it to the inclusive bounds; returns 0.0 for a null or empty array, and also if either bound is NaN. Reversed bounds are swapped; a NaN element makes the result NaN.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestValue
description: Returns the largest value, including when all values are negative. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestValue
description: Returns the smallest value, including when all values are positive or negative. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfLargest
description: Returns the index of the first largest value. Returns -1 for a null or empty array.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: countLargestValues
description: Returns how many times the largest value occurs; negative values are handled normally. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestValueInRows
description: Returns the smallest value among all non-null rows; null rows are ignored. Returns 0 if the outer array is null or there are no values.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestInList
description: Returns the largest non-null list element, including negative values. Returns 0 for a null or empty list, or if the list contains only null elements.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfLargestString
description: Returns the index of the lexicographically largest non-null string; an empty string is a valid value. Returns -1 for a null or empty array, or if every element is null.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfSmallest
description: Returns the index of the first smallest value. Returns -1 for a null or empty array; the loop stops early if it finds Integer.MIN_VALUE, which cannot be beaten.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: secondLargestDistinct
description: Returns the second-largest distinct value, or null if the array is null, empty, or has fewer than two distinct values. Negative values are handled normally.
code_b: public static Integer secondLargestDistinct(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return null; } int largest = 0; int secondLargest = 0; boolean hasLargest = false; boolean hasSecondLargest = false; for (int value : values) { if (!hasLargest || value > largest) { if (hasLargest) { secondLargest = largest; hasSecondLargest = true; } largest = value; hasLargest = true; } else if (value < largest && (!hasSecondLargest || value > secondLargest)) { secondLargest = value; hasSecondLargest = true; } } return hasSecondLargest ? secondLargest : null; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: rowWithLargestSum
description: Returns the index of the row with the largest sum, keeping the first row in a tie. Null rows are ignored, empty rows count as sum zero, and -1 is returned for a null matrix or one with no non-null rows.
code_b: public static int rowWithLargestSum(int[][] matrix) { if (matrix == null) { return -1; } int bestRow = -1; int largestSum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < matrix.length; i++) { if (matrix[i] != null) { int sum = 0; for (int value : matrix[i]) { sum += value; } if (bestRow == -1 || sum > largestSum) { largestSum = sum; bestRow = i; } } } return bestRow; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestCharacter
description: Returns the smallest character in the array. Returns '\u0000' for a null or empty array; that character may also be a valid array value.
code_b: public static char smallestCharacter(char[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return (char) 0; } char smallest = values[0]; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < smallest) { smallest = values[i]; } } return smallest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestNonNullString
description: Returns the lexicographically smallest non-null string, or null if the array is null, empty, or contains no non-null strings. Empty strings are considered valid values.
code_b: public static String smallestNonNullString(String[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return null; } String smallest = null; for (String value : values) { if (value != null && (smallest == null || value.compareTo(smallest) < 0)) { smallest = value; } } return smallest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestEven
description: Returns the largest even value, or null for a null or empty array or an array with no even values. Negative even values are included.
code_b: public static Integer largestEven(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return null; } Integer largest = null; for (int value : values) { if (value % 2 == 0 && (largest == null || value > largest)) { largest = value; } } return largest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestPositive
description: Returns the smallest positive value, or null for a null or empty list or when there is no positive value. Null list elements are ignored.
code_b: public static Integer smallestPositive(List<Integer> values) { if (values == null || values.isEmpty()) { return null; } Integer smallest = null; for (Integer value : values) { if (value != null && value > 0 && (smallest == null || value < smallest)) { smallest = value; } } return smallest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: columnMaxima
description: Returns an array containing the maximum value in each column; rows shorter than a column are skipped, and ties do not affect the result. A null matrix, an empty matrix, or a matrix with only null or empty rows returns an empty array; null rows are ignored.
code_b: public static int[] columnMaxima(int[][] matrix) { if (matrix == null || matrix.length == 0) { return new int[0]; } int columnCount = 0; for (int[] row : matrix) { if (row != null && row.length > columnCount) { columnCount = row.length; } } int[] maxima = new int[columnCount]; boolean[] hasValue = new boolean[columnCount]; for (int[] row : matrix) { if (row != null) { for (int column = 0; column < row.length; column++) { if (!hasValue[column] || row[column] > maxima[column]) { maxima[column] = row[column]; hasValue[column] = true; } } } } return maxima; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestBeforeFirstNegative
description: Returns the largest value before the first negative value, stopping the scan at that negative value. Returns null for a null or empty array, or if the first value is negative; zero and other nonnegative values are included.
code_b: public static Integer largestBeforeFirstNegative(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return null; } Integer largest = null; for (int value : values) { if (value < 0) { break; } if (largest == null || value > largest) { largest = value; } } return largest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestMagnitude
description: Returns the greatest absolute magnitude, converting to long so Integer.MIN_VALUE is handled correctly. Returns 0 for a null or empty array.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfLongestString
description: Returns the index of the first longest non-null String. Returns -1 for a null or empty array, or when every element is null; empty Strings are valid and have length 0.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: rowOfLargestEntry
description: Returns the row index containing the first greatest entry, ignoring null and empty rows. Returns -1 for a null matrix or one with no entries; negative entries are handled normally.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexClosestToTarget
signature: public static int indexClosestToTarget(double[] values, double target)
description: Returns the first index whose value has the smallest absolute distance from target. Returns -1 for a null or empty array, a NaN target, or if no usable distance exists; NaN elements and NaN distances are skipped.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestInteriorPeak
description: Returns the greatest value that is strictly greater than both of its immediate neighbors; the first such value wins ties. Returns 0 for a null array or when there is no interior peak.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestAtEvenPositions
description: Returns the smallest value at an even index (0, 2, 4, and so on). Returns 0 for a null or empty array; negative values are considered normally.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestMainDiagonalValue
description: Returns the greatest available main-diagonal entry, where row and column indices are equal. Returns 0 for a null matrix or when no diagonal entry exists; null rows and rows too short for their diagonal entry are skipped.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestAdjacentRise
description: Returns the greatest difference between consecutive values, computed as the later value minus the earlier value; the result can be negative if every step decreases. Returns 0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two values.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: greatestNegative
description: Returns the greatest negative value (the one closest to zero), or 0 if values is null, empty, or contains no negative values.
code_b: public static int greatestNegative(int[] values) { if (values == null) return 0; boolean found = false; int greatest = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < 0 && (!found || values[i] > greatest)) { greatest = values[i]; found = true; } } return found ? greatest : 0; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestAtOddIndices
description: Returns the smallest value at an odd index (1, 3, 5, and so on), or 0 if values is null or has no odd indices.
code_b: public static int smallestAtOddIndices(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length < 2) return 0; int smallest = values[1]; for (int i = 3; i < values.length; i += 2) { if (values[i] < smallest) smallest = values[i]; } return smallest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfLargestBelow
signature: public static int indexOfLargestBelow(int[] values, int limit)
description: Returns the index of the first largest value strictly below limit, or -1 if values is null, empty, or has no qualifying value.
code_b: public static int indexOfLargestBelow(int[] values, int limit) { if (values == null) return -1; int index = -1; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < limit && (index == -1 || values[i] > values[index])) index = i; } return index; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestNonNaN
description: Returns the smallest value other than NaN; positive and negative infinity are included. Returns Double.NaN if values is null, empty, or contains only NaN values.
code_b: public static double smallestNonNaN(double[] values) { if (values == null) return Double.NaN; boolean found = false; double smallest = 0.0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (!Double.isNaN(values[i]) && (!found || values[i] < smallest)) { smallest = values[i]; found = true; } } return found ? smallest : Double.NaN; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestUpperTriangle
description: Returns the largest value at a position where the column index is at least the row index. Null arrays, null rows, and rows with no qualifying positions are ignored; returns 0 if no qualifying value exists.
code_b: public static int largestUpperTriangle(int[][] values) { if (values == null) return 0; boolean found = false; int largest = 0; for (int row = 0; row < values.length; row++) { if (values[row] != null) { for (int column = row; column < values[row].length; column++) { if (!found || values[row][column] > largest) { largest = values[row][column]; found = true; } } } } return found ? largest : 0; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: greatestCharacter
description: Returns the greatest char value in the array, or '\u0000' if values is null or empty.
code_b: public static char greatestCharacter(char[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) return (char) 0; char greatest = values[0]; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] > greatest) greatest = values[i]; } return greatest; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestMultipleOf
signature: public static int largestMultipleOf(int[] values, int divisor)
description: Returns the largest value divisible by divisor. Returns 0 if values is null or empty, divisor is 0, or no value is divisible by divisor.
code_b: public static int largestMultipleOf(int[] values, int divisor) { if (values == null || values.length == 0 || divisor == 0) return 0; boolean found = false; int largest = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] % divisor == 0 && (!found || values[i] > largest)) { largest = values[i]; found = true; } } return found ? largest : 0; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestValueWithOddFrequency
description: Returns the smallest distinct value that occurs an odd number of times, or 0 if values is null, empty, or has no such value.
code_b: public static int smallestValueWithOddFrequency(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) return 0; boolean found = false; int smallest = 0; for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { boolean seenBefore = false; for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) { if (values[j] == values[i]) seenBefore = true; } if (!seenBefore) { int count = 0; for (int j = 0; j < values.length; j++) { if (values[j] == values[i]) count++; } if (count % 2 == 1 && (!found || values[i] < smallest)) { smallest = values[i]; found = true; } } } return found ? smallest : 0; }

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestAtIndicesMultipleOfThree
description: Returns the largest value at an index divisible by 3, including index 0. Returns 0 for a null or empty array; 0 also means there were no qualifying indices.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestAtPrimeIndices
description: Returns the smallest value at a prime-numbered index (2, 3, 5, and so on). Returns 0 for a null or empty array, or when the array has no prime-numbered index.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfLargestOddValue
description: Returns the index of the first occurrence of the largest odd value. Returns -1 for a null or empty array, or when no odd value is present.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: indexOfSmallestRepeatedValue
description: Returns the first index of the smallest value that occurs at least twice. Returns -1 for a null or empty array, or when every value occurs only once.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestValueAppearingOnce
description: Returns the largest value that occurs exactly once. Returns 0 for a null or empty array, or when no value occurs exactly once; 0 may also be a valid result.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestFiniteValue
description: Returns the largest finite value, ignoring NaN and positive or negative infinity. Returns NaN for a null or empty array, or when the array contains no finite values.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: smallestBorderValue
description: Returns the smallest value on the border of the matrix: in its first or last row, or at the first or last position of its row. Null rows and empty rows contribute no values. Returns 0 for a null matrix or when it contains no border values.

topic: finding the largest or smallest value, or its position, in an array (values may be negative)
name: largestInBounds
signature: public static int largestInBounds(List<Integer> values, int lower, int upper)
description: Returns the largest non-null list value between lower and upper, inclusive. Ignores null elements and returns 0 for a null or empty list, when lower is greater than upper, or when no value is in bounds; 0 may also be a valid result.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsInt
signature: public static boolean containsInt(int[] values, int target)
description: Returns true if the array contains target, otherwise false. A null or empty array is treated as empty and returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfChar
signature: public static int indexOfChar(String text, char target)
description: Returns the index of the first target character, or -1 if it is not found. A null or empty String is treated as empty and returns -1.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allPositive
description: Returns true if every array value is greater than zero. A null or empty array is treated as empty, so this method returns true.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyEven
description: Returns true if the list contains an even number, otherwise false. A null list is treated as empty, and null list elements are ignored; an empty list returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsWordIgnoreCase
signature: public static boolean containsWordIgnoreCase(String[] words, String target)
description: Returns true if an array entry equals target without regard to case. A null array is treated as empty, a null target returns false, and null entries are skipped; an empty array returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allNonEmptyStrings
description: Returns true if every entry is non-null and has at least one character. A null or empty array is treated as empty and returns true; a null or empty entry returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsInRows
signature: public static boolean containsInRows(int[][] rows, int target)
description: Returns true if any non-null row contains target. A null or empty outer array is treated as empty, null rows are skipped, and the result is false if no match is found.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: hasBothSigns
description: Returns true if the array contains at least one positive and at least one negative value. A null or empty array returns false; zero and NaN values do not count as either sign.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsExact
signature: public static boolean containsExact(List<String> words, String target)
description: Returns false for a null or empty list. Matches strings exactly and case-sensitively; a null target matches a null list element.
code_b: public static boolean containsExact(List<String> words, String target) { if (words == null || words.isEmpty()) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) { String word = words.get(i); if (target == null ? word == null : target.equals(word)) { return true; } } return false; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstGreater
signature: public static int indexOfFirstGreater(int[] values, int limit)
description: Returns the index of the first value greater than limit, or -1 if there is no match. Returns -1 for a null or empty array.
code_b: public static int indexOfFirstGreater(int[] values, int limit) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return -1; } for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] > limit) { return i; } } return -1; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyTrue
description: Returns true if at least one element is true, and false otherwise. A null or empty array returns false.
code_b: public static boolean anyTrue(boolean[] flags) { if (flags == null || flags.length == 0) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < flags.length; i++) { if (flags[i]) { return true; } } return false; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allAtMost
signature: public static boolean allAtMost(double[] values, double limit)
description: Returns true if every value is at most limit; an empty array returns true, while a null array returns false. NaN values, or a NaN limit with a nonempty array, make the check return false.
code_b: public static boolean allAtMost(double[] values, double limit) { if (values == null) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (Double.isNaN(limit) || Double.isNaN(values[i]) || values[i] > limit) { return false; } } return true; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsCharacter
signature: public static boolean containsCharacter(String text, char target)
description: Returns true if text contains target, and false otherwise. A null or empty String returns false.
code_b: public static boolean containsCharacter(String text, char target) { if (text == null || text.isEmpty()) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < text.length(); i++) { if (text.charAt(i) == target) { return true; } } return false; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstNull
description: Returns the index of the first null element, or -1 if there is none. A null or empty array returns -1.
code_b: public static int indexOfFirstNull(String[] values) { if (values == null || values.length == 0) { return -1; } for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] == null) { return i; } } return -1; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyRowHasAdjacentEqual
description: Returns true if any non-null row contains equal values in two adjacent positions. A null or empty outer array returns false; null rows and rows with fewer than two elements are ignored.
code_b: public static boolean anyRowHasAdjacentEqual(int[][] rows) { if (rows == null || rows.length == 0) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) { if (rows[i] != null) { for (int j = 0; j < rows[i].length - 1; j++) { if (rows[i][j] == rows[i][j + 1]) { return true; } } } } return false; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allWithinRange
signature: public static boolean allWithinRange(int[] values, int low, int high)
description: Returns true if every value is between low and high, inclusive; an empty array returns true, while a null array returns false. If low is greater than high, every nonempty array returns false.
code_b: public static boolean allWithinRange(int[] values, int low, int high) { if (values == null) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (low > high || values[i] < low || values[i] > high) { return false; } } return true; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsSubstring
signature: public static boolean containsSubstring(String text, String part)
description: Returns whether text contains part; null text or part returns false. An empty part matches any non-null text, including an empty String.
code_b: public static boolean containsSubstring(String text, String part) { if (text == null || part == null) { return false; } return text.indexOf(part) >= 0; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfLast
signature: public static int indexOfLast(int[] values, int target)
description: Returns the last index containing target, or -1 if it is not found. A null or empty array returns -1.
code_b: public static int indexOfLast(int[] values, int target) { if (values == null) { return -1; } for (int i = values.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { if (values[i] == target) { return i; } } return -1; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allCharsEqual
signature: public static boolean allCharsEqual(String text, char expected)
description: Returns true if every character equals expected; an empty String returns true. A null String returns false.
code_b: public static boolean allCharsEqual(String text, char expected) { if (text == null) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < text.length(); i++) { if (text.charAt(i) != expected) { return false; } } return true; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyInRange
signature: public static boolean anyInRange(double[] values, double low, double high)
description: Returns true if any value is between low and high, inclusive; otherwise returns false. A null or empty array, or low greater than high, returns false; NaN values do not match.
code_b: public static boolean anyInRange(double[] values, double low, double high) { if (values == null || values.length == 0 || low > high) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] >= low && values[i] <= high) { return true; } } return false; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allStartWith
signature: public static boolean allStartWith(String[] words, String prefix)
description: Returns true if every element starts with prefix; a null or empty array returns true. For a nonempty array, a null prefix or any null element makes the result false; an empty prefix matches every non-null element.
code_b: public static boolean allStartWith(String[] words, String prefix) { if (words == null || words.length == 0) { return true; } if (prefix == null) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < words.length; i++) { if (words[i] == null || !words[i].startsWith(prefix)) { return false; } } return true; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyNegative
description: Returns true if any non-null list element is negative; otherwise returns false. A null list is treated as empty, and null elements are ignored.
code_b: public static boolean anyNegative(List<Integer> values) { if (values == null) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < values.size(); i++) { Integer value = values.get(i); if (value != null && value < 0) { return true; } } return false; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstLongerThan
signature: public static int indexOfFirstLongerThan(String[] words, int minLength)
description: Returns the first index of a non-null String whose length is greater than minLength, or -1 if none matches. A null or empty array returns -1, and null elements are skipped.
code_b: public static int indexOfFirstLongerThan(String[] words, int minLength) { if (words == null) { return -1; } for (int i = 0; i < words.length; i++) { if (words[i] != null && words[i].length() > minLength) { return i; } } return -1; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allRowsContainValue
signature: public static boolean allRowsContainValue(int[][] rows, int target)
description: Returns true if every row contains target; a null or empty outer array returns true. A null row or empty row returns false because it cannot contain target.
code_b: public static boolean allRowsContainValue(int[][] rows, int target) { if (rows == null || rows.length == 0) { return true; } for (int i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) { if (rows[i] == null || rows[i].length == 0) { return false; } boolean found = false; for (int j = 0; j < rows[i].length; j++) { if (rows[i][j] == target) { found = true; break; } } if (!found) { return false; } } return true; }

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsAsciiDigit
description: Returns true if the String contains an ASCII digit from '0' through '9'. A null or empty String returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstSpaceOrTab
description: Returns the index of the first space or tab, or -1 if neither occurs. A null or empty String returns -1.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyNull
description: Returns true as soon as it finds a null element. A null or empty array returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allStrictlyIncreasing
description: Returns true if every element is greater than the element before it. A null or empty array, and an array with one element, return true.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: hasDuplicate
description: Returns true if any two elements have the same value, stopping when it finds a duplicate. A null or empty array returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstUppercase
description: Returns the index of the first ASCII uppercase letter, or -1 if none is present. A null or empty array returns -1.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: anyRowIsEmpty
description: Returns true if any row is null or has length zero. A null or empty outer array returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allRowsSameLength
description: Returns true if all rows have the same length, treating a null row as having length zero. A null or empty outer array returns true.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstEven
description: Returns the index of the first even value, or -1 if none is found. A null or empty array returns -1.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsIgnoreCase
signature: public static boolean containsIgnoreCase(String[] values, String target)
description: Returns true if a non-null element matches target without regard to letter case. A null array or target returns false; null elements are ignored, and an empty array returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: allDivisibleBy
signature: public static boolean allDivisibleBy(int[] values, int divisor)
description: Returns true if every value is divisible by divisor; a divisor of zero returns false. A null array returns false, while an empty array returns true for any nonzero divisor.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: hasAdjacentIncrease
description: Returns true if any value is greater than the value immediately before it. A null array or an array with fewer than two elements returns false.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstNonzero
description: Returns the index of the first nonzero value, or -1 if none is found. A null or empty array returns -1.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: hasPairWithSum
signature: public static boolean hasPairWithSum(int[] values, int target)
description: Returns true if two different array elements add up to target. A null array or an array with fewer than two elements returns false; sums are checked using long arithmetic to avoid integer overflow.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: containsAllRequiredValues
signature: public static boolean containsAllRequiredValues(int[] values, int[] required)
description: Returns true if each value in required appears at least once in values; repeated required values do not require repeated matches. If either array is null, returns false; an empty required array returns true when values is non-null.

topic: searching: contains, indexOf, all-match and any-match checks that return as soon as they know
name: indexOfFirstAsciiAlphanumeric
description: Returns the index of the first ASCII letter or digit, or -1 if none is found. A null or empty string returns -1.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: isNondecreasing
description: Returns true if every element is at least the one before it; arrays of length 0 or 1 are sorted. A null array is treated as empty and returns true.
code_b: public static boolean isNondecreasing(int[] values) { if (values == null) return true; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < values[i - 1]) return false; } return true; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countRises
description: Returns the number of neighbouring pairs where the second value is greater than the first. Returns 0 for an empty or one-element array; a null array is treated as empty.
code_b: public static int countRises(int[] values) { if (values == null) return 0; int count = 0; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] > values[i - 1]) count++; } return count; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: biggestJump
description: Returns the largest absolute difference between neighbouring values. Returns 0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.
code_b: public static long biggestJump(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length < 2) return 0; long biggest = 0; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { long difference = (long) values[i] - values[i - 1]; if (difference < 0) difference = -difference; if (difference > biggest) biggest = difference; } return biggest; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: hasAdjacentEqual
description: Returns true if any two neighbouring characters are equal. Returns false for a null array or an array with fewer than two characters.
code_b: public static boolean hasAdjacentEqual(char[] values) { if (values == null) return false; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] == values[i - 1]) return true; } return false; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: firstDropIndex
description: Returns the index of the first element that is smaller than the element immediately before it. Returns -1 if there is no such pair, including when the array is null or has fewer than two elements.
code_b: public static int firstDropIndex(int[] values) { if (values == null) return -1; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] < values[i - 1]) return i; } return -1; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countStringChanges
description: Counts neighbouring pairs of strings that differ, using case-sensitive comparison; two null entries count as equal, while one null and one non-null entry count as different. Returns 0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two entries.
code_b: public static int countStringChanges(String[] values) { if (values == null) return 0; int count = 0; for (int i = 1; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] == null) { if (values[i - 1] != null) count++; } else if (!values[i].equals(values[i - 1])) { count++; } } return count; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countRisingPairs
description: Counts neighbouring pairs of non-null integers where the second is greater than the first. A null list or a list with fewer than two elements returns 0; a null element breaks the neighbouring comparison across it.
code_b: public static int countRisingPairs(List<Integer> values) { if (values == null || values.size() < 2) return 0; int count = 0; for (int i = 1; i < values.size(); i++) { Integer previous = values.get(i - 1); Integer current = values.get(i); if (previous != null && current != null && current > previous) count++; } return count; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countRowsWithRise
description: Counts rows that contain at least one neighbouring pair where the second value is greater than the first. A null outer array is treated as empty; null rows and rows with fewer than two values do not count.
code_b: public static int countRowsWithRise(int[][] rows) { if (rows == null) return 0; int count = 0; for (int i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) { if (rows[i] != null) { for (int j = 1; j < rows[i].length; j++) { if (rows[i][j] > rows[i][j - 1]) { count++; break; } } } } return count; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: isNonincreasing
description: Returns true if each value is less than or equal to the previous value. Null and empty arrays return true.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: longestIncreasingRun
description: Returns the number of elements in the longest contiguous run where each element is strictly greater than the previous one. Null and empty arrays return 0.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countLocalMaxima
description: Counts elements that are strictly greater than both immediate neighbours; the first and last elements are not considered. Null arrays and arrays shorter than three elements return 0.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countDirectionChanges
description: Counts switches between rising and falling adjacent steps, ignoring equal neighbouring values. Null arrays and arrays with fewer than two elements return 0.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: sumAbsoluteAdjacentDifferences
description: Returns the sum of the absolute differences between every neighbouring pair. Null arrays and arrays with fewer than two elements return 0.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: firstPairWithSum
signature: public static int firstPairWithSum(int[] values, int target)
description: Returns the starting index of the first neighbouring pair whose sum equals target, or -1 if no such pair exists. Null arrays and arrays with fewer than two elements return -1.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentPairsWithUniqueEndpoints
description: Counts neighbouring pairs for which each endpoint value occurs exactly once in the entire array. Null arrays and arrays with fewer than two elements return 0.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentSumsDivisibleByThree
description: Returns the number of neighboring pairs whose sum is divisible by three. Returns 0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: hasAdjacentOppositeSigns
description: Returns true if any neighboring pair contains one negative and one positive value; zero is neither. Returns false for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: smallestAdjacentSum
description: Returns the smallest sum of any neighboring pair. Returns Long.MAX_VALUE for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentPairsWithIncreasingMagnitude
description: Counts neighboring pairs where the right value has a greater absolute magnitude than the left value. Returns 0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentWordsStartingWithSameLetter
description: Counts neighboring non-null, non-empty words that start with the same case-sensitive character. A null or empty array returns 0; a null or empty word breaks the comparison between its neighbors.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentIdenticalRows
description: Counts neighboring rows with identical contents; null rows are treated as empty rows, so a null row matches an empty row. Returns 0 for a null outer array or an array with fewer than two rows.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: sumAdjacentProducts
description: Returns the sum of the products of all neighboring pairs, using double arithmetic. Returns 0.0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentPairsWithExactlyOneZero
description: Counts neighboring pairs where exactly one value is zero. Returns 0 for a null array or an array with fewer than two elements.

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: isAlternatingSigns
description: Returns false for null, or if any value is zero; otherwise returns true when every neighbouring pair has opposite signs. An empty array returns true.
code_b: public static boolean isAlternatingSigns(int[] values) { if (values == null) { return false; } for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { if (values[i] == 0) { return false; } if (i > 0 && ((values[i] > 0) == (values[i - 1] > 0))) { return false; } } return true; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: maxAdjacentProduct
description: Returns the greatest product of any neighbouring pair, using long arithmetic. Returns 0 for null arrays or arrays with fewer than two elements.
code_b: public static long maxAdjacentProduct(int[] values) { if (values == null || values.length < 2) { return 0; } long greatest = (long) values[0] * values[1]; for (int i = 1; i < values.length - 1; i++) { long product = (long) values[i] * values[i + 1]; if (product > greatest) { greatest = product; } } return greatest; }

topic: comparing neighbouring elements: is the array sorted, count rises, biggest jump, pairs a[i] and a[i + 1]
name: countAdjacentVowelPairs
description: Counts neighbouring pairs in which both characters are English vowels, ignoring letter case; y is not counted as a vowel. Returns 0 for null, empty, or one-character strings.
